Test isolates each run's store — point `HOME` (or the store path, whichever TASK-002
ac_results.evidence: test/cli.test.js: freshHome() uses fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'todo-cli-integration-test-')) per test; run() spawns bin/todo.js with env HOME/USERPROFILE overridden to that temp dir. lib/todo-repository.js storePath() = path.join(os.homedir(), '.todo.json'), which resolves HOME in the child's env, so the real user's ~/.todo.json is never touched.

assumptions: Interpreted the 4 BDD scenarios (happy-path round-trip, empty list, bad index x4 invocations, corrupted store x4 invocations) as the concrete observable checks backing the two baseline AC checkboxes; all 4 are implemented as node:test cases in test/cli.test.js and all pass.

Corrupted-store stderr check asserts /corrupt/i is present (matches todo-repository.js's existing 'todo store is corrupted' message) and asserts SyntaxError/stack-trace text is absent, per the AC's 'no raw SyntaxError/stack-trace text' requirement.
